newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt remains firm but buyers largely absent.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt remains firm but buyers largely absent.

text.p: Emerging debt prices remained firm on Wednesday after Tuesday's rally triggered by favourable U.S. inflation data.
Dealers said the market was up by around 1/2 point on average, but this was not seen as a sign of a lasting market turnaround.
"The market is still firm but volumes are light," a dealer at a European bank said.
"Russia and Bulgaria are up a bit more than other paper because traders are still short-covering from Tuesday," he said.
The market would remain focused on moves in U.S. Treasuries, another dealer said, which have been volatile due to uncertaintly surrounding possible rises in interest rates.
"Bradys are still very technical, and still not reacting to country-specific news," a U.S. bank trader said.

"We expect the U.S. long bond may reach 7.25 percent in the next week or so, and such a move will drag Bradys down again. We are not advising investors to buy, but it may be a good time to sell," he said.
At 1100 GMT the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was quoted at a 7.09 percent yield, unchanged from the New York close on Tuesday. -- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
